summary: Plan nonsplitting Hurwitz-space homological stability from the component monoid and topological Hurwitz covers of the parent roadmap. Build the actual central sum, the graded K-complex and its degree estimates, the truncated arc resolution and its spectral sequence, and the induction for marked, full-monodromy and unmarked spaces. Combine linear stability and a finite-cell bound with the parent fixed-n comparison to obtain a uniform etale Betti estimate. General topology, mapping-class carriers and graded derived tensor products remain with their existing owners, with precise requests for missing interfaces.

conventions: G is a finite group, c is a nonempty single G-conjugacy class, and k is a field with |G| nonzero in k. Nonsplitting includes generation. Topological constructions of the ring and K use only a conjugacy class; their degree theorems impose nonsplitting.

Hur_n denotes the marked c-valued disc Hurwitz cover, including nongenerating tuples and every boundary product; CHur_n is its full-monodromy subcover. A slash G means the ordinary simultaneous-conjugation quotient. These are the four distinct spaces imported from IG.5. No product-one restriction is imposed.

Classical braid generators sigma_1,...,sigma_(n-1) correspond to TauCeti.BraidGroup.sigma with indices 0,...,n-2. B_0 and B_1 are trivial. The left Hurwitz move sends (g,h) to (g h g^-1,g); exponent g^h means h^-1 g h.

All internal gradings are nonnegative, and all modules in the degree estimates are nonnegatively graded (or given a specified common lower bound and shifted first). Internal shift M[q]_n is M_(n-q), with zero below q. Homological degree q is separate. Internal grading introduces no Koszul signs.

A degree assertion deg V <= b means V_n=0 for every integer n>b. Zero has degree minus infinity and unbounded support has degree plus infinity; displayed bounds with finite degrees are proved on support, with zero cases handled separately. Constants are nonnegative integers.

d is the common positive order of the elements of c. Fix a combinatorially admissible D>=1 from component stability, a=Dd, U=sum_(g in c) r_g^(Dd). Choose A1>=max(1,a,deg R[U],deg R/UR) uniformly over permitted fields, A2=A1+a, A0=5A1+A2. This enlargement repairs EVW Proposition4.13.

Tor_i^R(N,M) uses a graded RIGHT R-module N followed by a graded LEFT R-module M. Balanced tensor products over R are noncommutative; ordinary Mathlib TensorProduct is used only over k. The generic graded module, balanced tensor and derived machinery belong to DGAInfinity.

The arc semisimplicial set has q-simplices only for 0<=q<n. Its augmentation is a point in degree -1. K(M) has all homological degrees q>=0. The spectral sequence is nonaugmented: its zeroth column on E2 is coker(K2->K1), not H1(K).

U acts on homology as a k-linear sum of gluing operators. It is not asserted to come from one map of spaces or an algebraic stabilization morphism. The etale output is a dimension bound using fixed-degree comparisons and an auxiliary prime L, without Frobenius-equivariant stabilization.

nodes.title: Nonsplitting conjugacy classes
nodes.statement: For a subset c of a group G, Nonsplitting(c) means: c is one nonempty whole G-conjugacy class, its generated subgroup is G, and for every subgroup H<=G the intersection c∩H is empty or one H-conjugacy class. Equivalently, after the first two conditions, any g,h in c∩H are conjugate by an element of H. The intersection is automatically H-conjugation invariant.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Use native conjugacy and subgroup closure. Translate the intersection condition into a pairwise-conjugacy predicate, retaining the ambient whole-class condition.
For H with c∩H generating H, transport the same predicate to the subtype H; only such H contribute to exact-monodromy tuples.
acceptance: A union of distinct ambient conjugacy classes is rejected even if it generates.

sources.match: Defines the subgroup intersection condition; the target retains the whole generating ambient class and makes its pairwise reformulation explicit.

nodes.statement: If |G|=2s with s odd, the elements of order2 form one conjugacy class c. If c generates G, then c is nonsplitting. In particular the transposition class of S3 satisfies the stability hypotheses.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.

Every subgroup containing an involution has the same order shape; apply Sylow conjugacy in that subgroup. Then add the stipulated generation.

nodes.title: Gluing of marked Hurwitz covers
nodes.statement: Use the parent Borel models Hur_n=EB_n×_(B_n)c^n. Block inclusion B_n×B_m->B_(n+m) and concatenation c^n×c^m->c^(n+m) induce gluing Hur_n×Hur_m->Hur_(n+m), associative and unital up to compatible homotopies, equivariant for simultaneous G-conjugation. The external homology cross product followed by gluing yields the graded homology multiplication. It preserves the c-valued condition and sends monodromy subgroups H,K to <H,K>.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Use block inclusions and tuple concatenation on classifying constructions, with the functorial homotopies provided by Borel realization.
Apply the singular cross product and its associativity/unit compatibility. Degree-zero multiplication is concatenation of braid orbits.

nodes.title: The graded component ring
nodes.statement: Import S=disjoint_union_n c^n/B_n with concatenation from IG.3, and define R as native MonoidAlgebra k S. Give it the length grading R_n=k[S_n], augmentation R->k projecting to R_0=k, G-action by conjugation, and boundary G-grading. Set r_g=single([g],1). Its presentation is the free associative k-algebra on r_g (g∈c) modulo r_g r_h=r_(g h g^-1) r_g. Gluing identifies R with direct_sum_n H_0(Hur_n;k), as a graded algebra.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Use the native monoid algebra of the imported monoid; length is invariant under its defining Hurwitz relations.
The braid generators and their inverses generate precisely the orbit congruence, yielding the presentation; compare degree-zero singular homology of a covering with its components.

nodes.title: Stability on components
nodes.statement: If c is nonsplitting, there are D>=1 and N>=0 depending only on (G,c), such that U_D:R_n->R_(n+a) is an isomorphism for every n>=N and every coefficient field in which |G| is invertible. Thus R[U_D] and R/U_DR have finite support. D may be chosen simultaneously for all nonempty generating intersections c∩H in subgroups H, and any positive multiple of the resulting permutation exponent is admissible after increasing N.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Fix exact-monodromy subsets S_n(H). If nonempty, c∩H generates H and is a single H-class. Repeated parent extraction gives eventual surjectivity of multiplication by each z_g, hence eventual bijectivity and bounded cardinalities on each residue class modulo d. There are finitely many H and residues.

Commuting z_g maps identify their ratios with permutations of bounded finite sets. Choose one exponent D killing all those permutations. The diagonal actions z_g^D on each stable S_n(H) then coincide.

Filter R by subgroup order at least m. U is triangular; on the exact-H graded piece it is |c∩H| times a bijection. This cardinal divides |H| and is a unit in k. Descend on m. All thresholds and permutation bounds are chosen before coefficients, giving field independence.
acceptance: Use cardinality stabilization, not the assertion that a surjection between two finite sets is automatically a bijection.
c∩H may fail to generate H only when every S_n(H) is empty.
For trivial G one may take D=1,N=0, although R/U has degree0 and the corrected A1 is still at least1.

The internal shift M[q] has M[q]_n=M_(n-q), zero if n<q; a homogeneous map of degree a is a degree-zero map M[a]->N. Homological complexes retain a distinct nonnegative chain index. The native GradedObject supplies the family carrier; module structures and shift functors are imported from DGAInfinity.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Express every numerical inequality as a finite support cutoff before introducing degree notation. Transport the internal shift from the supplier, avoiding its cohomological shift and Koszul sign conventions.
Verify exact sequences give the maximum support bound and finite direct sums give the maximum of summand degrees.
acceptance: The zero family is supported below every cutoff; no artificial degree0 is assigned to it.

nodes.statement: For a graded left R-module M let M[U]=ker(U:M->M), regarded in the source grading, and M/UM the cokernel in the target grading. Choose A1>=max(1,a,A(R)), A2=A1+a, A0=5A1+A2. Finite support of these defects is the meaning of eventual U-stability, with separate source and target cutoffs.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Take the homogeneous kernel and cokernel using the imported abelian category of graded modules and the balanced right/left Tor interface.
Use component stability to choose a uniform nonnegative A1 at least a and at least1; do not insist on the source equality A1=A(R).

nodes.statement: For a nonnegative graded right R-module N and left R-module M, deg(N tensor_R M)<=deg N+deg H_0^aug(M), whenever the right side is finite; the zero cases vanish. The same statement holds for the central quotient Rbar.

proofSteps: Filter a bounded N by internal degree from the top. Each associated graded is a sum of shifted augmentation modules k, since positive-degree elements raise degree.
Use right exactness of the balanced tensor and the support bound in exact sequences. Reduce the nonzero finite-support case to N=k shifted.

nodes.title: Bounding central torsion by quotient Tor
nodes.statement: For every nonnegative graded left R-module M, A(M)<=delta(M)+A1. More precisely there is an exact-at-the-middle sequence R[U] tensor_R M -> M[U] -> Tor_1^R(Rbar,M), whose first map has internal degree0 and second map has internal degree a.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Factor U:M->M through UR tensor_R M. Tensor the sequences R[U]->R->UR and UR->R->Rbar, keeping their homogeneous degrees.
The first kernel is an image of R[U] tensor_R M; the second is Tor_1^R(Rbar,M). Apply the tensor bound and deg H_0^aug(M)<=deg M/UM<=delta(M). The nonnegative degree a allows the conservative bound.

nodes.title: Higher central-quotient Tor estimates
nodes.statement: For i>=0 and nonnegative graded left R-module M, deg Tor_i^R(Rbar,M)<=delta(M)+A1 i.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: R[U] is a right Rbar-module. Resolve it by free right Rbar-modules Q_j with generators in degrees <=(j+1)A1. Splice Q into R[U]->R->R->Rbar, inserting the internal shifts that make the U map degree0.

Use the supplier hyperhomology spectral sequence of this homogeneous right R-complex tensored with M. The spliced resolution has P0=R, P1=R[a], and Pj=Q_(j-2)[a] for j>=2. For total degree b>=2, a piece with 0<=u<=b-2 has generator shift <=(b-u-1)A1+a and inner Tor_u^R(Rbar,M). Since a<=A1, induction bounds it by delta(M)+b A1. This makes explicit the shifts suppressed in the source display (E6).
acceptance: i=0,1 are controlled directly by delta; shifts in the two R terms must not be discarded.

nodes.title: Graded Nakayama with support control
nodes.statement: For every nonnegative graded left Rbar-module V with finite degree of k tensor_Rbar V, deg V<=deg(k tensor_Rbar V)+deg Rbar. In particular k tensor_Rbar V=0 implies V=0.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Lift a homogeneous k-basis of augmentation coinvariants. The quotient by the module these lifts generate has zero coinvariants.
A least nonzero internal degree of that quotient cannot be in its positive-ideal multiple, so the quotient is zero. Bound degrees of the resulting generators using finite support of Rbar.
acceptance: A lower bound on grading is essential; unrestricted integer-graded modules cannot be substituted.

nodes.title: Low augmentation Tor controls the defect
nodes.statement: For every nonnegative graded left R-module M, delta(M)<=max(deg H_0^aug(M),deg H_1^aug(M))+4A1.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: The zeroth quotient Tor has degree <=deg H_0^aug(M)+deg Rbar.
Use the change-of-rings low exact segment; apply graded Nakayama to Tor_1^R(Rbar,M), then the quotient Tor bound with i=2. This contributes at most four copies of deg Rbar.
acceptance: For R=k[t],M=k, delta=1 and the chosen A1>=1 gives a valid bound.

nodes.title: A general right-module Tor bound
nodes.statement: If N is a nonnegative graded right R-module and M a nonnegative graded left R-module, then deg Tor_i^R(N,M)<=deg N+max(deg H_0^aug(M),deg H_1^aug(M))+A1 i+4A1, for all i>=0 with finite displayed degree bounds.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Filter finite-support N by top internal degree and use Tor long exact sequences, reducing to shifted sums of k.
For N=k, total degree i in change of rings has a+b=i. The inner and outer bounds give a deg Rbar+b A1+delta(M), hence A1 i plus the low-Tor defect estimate.
acceptance: No commutativity or global finite projective dimension of R is asserted.

nodes.title: The Hurwitz K-complex
nodes.statement: For a nonnegative graded left R-module M define a homological complex K(M) with K(M)_q=k[c^q] tensor_k M[q] for every q>=0. On a basis tensor with (q+1)-tuple (g_0,...,g_q), d sends it to sum_i (-1)^i (g_0,...,omit g_i,...,g_q) tensor r_(g_i^(g_(i+1)...g_q)) m. The empty suffix is1. Differential preserves internal grading and lowers chain degree by1. Degree-zero R-linear maps of M induce chain maps. For M=R this is a complex of free graded right R-modules.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Construct finite free coefficient modules on c^q over k and use the imported internal shifts; no truncation in q is introduced.
Pair the two orders of deletion to prove d squared zero, using r_h r_(h^-1 g h)=r_g r_h. Left multiplication on R commutes with its right regular action.
acceptance: All suffix conjugations follow g^h=h^-1 g h, rather than the opposite action.

nodes.title: Null-homotopies for positive generators
nodes.statement: For g∈c define a k-linear homotopy S_g on the tuple-orbit basis of K(R). For a tuple w of length q and monoid basis element s with boundary b, put S_g(w;s)=(g^((boundary(w)b)^-1),w;s). It raises chain degree and internal degree by1, extends linearly in s, and satisfies d S_g+S_g d = right multiplication by r_g. No right R-linearity of S_g is required or claimed.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.

Compute the first deletion as the right multiplication term using the Hurwitz relation; match all other deletions against S_g d with opposite signs. Include chain degree0 in this calculation.

nodes.title: The positive ideal kills regular K-homology
nodes.statement: For every q>=0, the graded right R-module H_q(K(R)) is annihilated by R_positive. In particular right multiplication by U, and hence its equal left action on coefficients, is zero on homology.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Each r_g acts trivially by its explicit chain homotopy. Since the r_g generate the positive ideal, every positive-degree element acts trivially.
U is positive-degree and central, so its left coefficient action is its right action.
acceptance: Annihilation holds on homology, while the coefficient multiplication chain map need not be zero.

nodes.title: Regular K-homology has linear support
nodes.statement: For every q>=0, deg H_q(K(R))<=A2+q. In particular the first two K-homology groups of R have finite degree.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: U is an isomorphism on K(R)_q in source internal degrees above A1+q. Use the neighboring terms to obtain the same bound on cycles.

Repeatedly divide a cycle by U in the stable degrees to generate its cycle module in degrees <=A1+a+q. The quotient homology is killed by positive R, so generation in that range becomes a support bound.

nodes.statement: For M as above, the right-free complex K(R) gives a first-quadrant spectral sequence E2_(i,j)=Tor_i^R(H_j(K(R)),M) converging to H_(i+j)(K(M)), preserving internal grading. Consequently deg H_q(K(M))<=max(deg H_0^aug(M),deg H_1^aug(M))+A1 q+4A1+A2. This bound uses the chosen A1>=1.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Specialize the supplier hyperhomology comparison to the right-free complex K(R) and a free left resolution of M. The tensor comparison identifies the abutment.
At i+j=q apply the general Tor bound and regular K bound. The resulting term j+A1 i is <=A1 q precisely because A1>=1. First-quadrant diagonals are finite even though K is unbounded above.

nodes.title: The marked-disc braid adapter
nodes.statement: For the oriented compact smooth disc with n interior marked points, take orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms fixing the boundary pointwise and preserving the marked set setwise. Import their C-infinity topological group from GeometricTopology and their isotopy-class mapping group from the mapping-class supplier. Construct the compatible isomorphisms pi_0 Diff^+(D,P;boundary) ≅ Mod(D,P;boundary) ≅ TauCeti.BraidGroup n ≅ pi_1(Conf_n). A native sigma_i corresponds to the positive half twist interchanging the two adjacent marked points; pure mapping classes and full twists are different.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Use the parent configuration/braid comparison and the supplier disc point-pushing comparison between isotopies of marked diffeomorphisms and loops of unordered configurations. The required smooth/topological relative comparison is an explicit supplier request.
Normalize on adjacent half twists and verify compatibility with the parent left Hurwitz action, boundary fixation and block inclusion. Include n=0,1 separately.

nodes.title: The based arc complex
nodes.statement: Fix a boundary basepoint star on D and n distinct interior points P. A vertex is the isotopy class relative to star and P of a smooth embedded arc from star to one marked point, with interior in int(D) minus P and inward non-tangent initial derivative. A q-simplex is a collection of q+1 such classes with representatives disjoint away from star and with distinct marked endpoints and distinct ordered inward tangent rays near star. Order the vertices by their counterclockwise rays at star. Deleting an arc gives its semisimplicial faces. There are no q-simplices for q>=n. Orientation-preserving boundary-fixed marked diffeomorphisms act, and the action descends to B_n through the disc adapter.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Use the supplier smooth embedding/isotopy carriers and take their relative isotopy quotient. The disjoint-realization condition defines a simplicial complex; ordered tangent rays give the semisimplicial ordering.
Show the ordering is isotopy independent for disjoint classes. Distinct endpoints imply the dimension bound; forgetting that condition would give another complex.
acceptance: Require simultaneous representatives, rather than pairwise disjointness asserted without representatives.

nodes.title: The truncated braid-coset model
nodes.statement: For n,q>=0 let L_(n,q) be the subgroup of B_n generated by the classical generators sigma_(q+2),...,sigma_(n-1). Empty generator ranges give the trivial subgroup; for q<n its shifted-strand inclusion identifies it with B_(n-q-1). Define A(n)_q=B_n/L_(n,q) if q<n and the empty set if q>=n. The quotient is by left cosets, with B_n acting by left multiplication. For q>=1 and q<n define s_(q,i)=sigma_(i+1)...sigma_q and face_i(bL_q)=b s_(q,i)L_(q-1), 0<=i<=q; s_(q,q)=1. Add the unique augmentation A(n)_0->point.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Generate the native subgroup from exactly the tail indices, converting classical to zero-based indexing. Form native subgroup quotients only in the permitted dimensions.

Prove the shifted inclusion is injective using the parent configuration-space braid comparison. Put m=n-q-1 moving points in a smaller disc, and keep the first q+1 points outside it. Lift a nullhomotopy in the unordered n-point configuration space to the finite cover recording which m points form the moving block; forget the other block. This gives a nullhomotopy in the m-point configuration space of the full disc. Inclusion of the smaller disc induces a homotopy equivalence on these configuration spaces, by a shrinking isotopy, so the original m-strand loop was null. For m=0,1 both source braid groups are trivial. Its image is exactly the subgroup generated by the shifted adjacent half twists.
Use products in increasing classical index; define faces only when their source exists. The following node proves well-definedness and the semisimplicial laws.

nodes.statement: The faces in the truncated coset model are independent of the representative and B_n-equivariant. For q>=2 and 0<=i<j<=q, face_i face_j=face_(j-1) face_i. Together with augmentation these make A(n) an augmented semisimplicial B_n-set, of dimension n-1 if n>0. No degeneracy maps are asserted.

proofSteps: L_q commutes with each sigma_j for j<=q, and L_q is included in L_(q-1); this proves well-definedness under b->b l.
For j=q cancel the additional sigma_q modulo L_(q-2). For j<q move it through the increasing products using adjacent braid relations, as in Proposition5.3. Empty top terms have unique faces.

nodes.title: Arc stabilizers and the coset identification
nodes.statement: For 0<=q<n, B_n acts transitively on ordered q-simplices of the geometric arc complex. The stabilizer of the standard fan of q+1 straight arcs is exactly L_(n,q). The maps bL_q -> b applied to the standard fan are equivariant bijections compatible with all faces and augmentation, hence identify the geometric and truncated coset semisimplicial sets.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Straighten two fans near the boundary and match endpoints by a marked-disc diffeomorphism. Use disjoint tubular neighborhoods and relative isotopy extension to carry one fan to the other.

For a diffeomorphism fixing all arc classes, fix representatives successively. In the cut punctured disc, remove intersections of the next arc isotopy with earlier arcs by innermost-circle surgery; the obstruction is pi_2 of the punctured cut disc, zero because it retracts to a graph. Request the needed relative smooth extension/cutting API explicitly.

After simultaneous pointwise fixing, isotope to the identity on a regular neighborhood of the fan. The remaining disc has n-q-1 punctures, so its image is the shifted tail subgroup. Conversely those tail braids fix the fan.
Compute deletion of the ith standard arc as s_(q,i) applied to the shorter fan, giving exactly the coset faces.
acceptance: A stabilizer of isotopy classes is not immediately a pointwise stabilizer; the simultaneous-straightening step is essential.

sources.match: Identifies the stabilizer of a standard arc system using the cut disc, after rectifying isotopies relative to the boundary and punctures.

nodes.title: Connectivity of the arc resolution
nodes.statement: For n>=1, the geometric arc realization, and hence |A(n)|, is (n-2)-connected. For n=1 the convention means nonempty; for n=2 it means path connected. For n=0 retain the explicitly empty complex. Only this connectivity, not a stronger contractibility assertion, is used.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Use the complex allowing repeated endpoints as a contractible surgery complex (Hatcher–Wahl Lemma7.1). In the disc case, put arcs in general position and push away intersections with a chosen arc via the first intersection surgery; simplicial approximation makes this a finite simplicial null-homotopy.

For a sphere of dimension <=n-2 in the distinct-endpoint subcomplex, choose an extension in the larger complex. Remove maximal bad simplices with repeated endpoints. The link is a join of smaller arc complexes in cut discs; induction and the dimension count in Hatcher–Wahl Proposition7.2 give the replacement extension.

Use simplicial approximation, the join-connectivity bound, and the relative extension criterion for connectivity from AlgebraicTopology. Record this precise join/simplicial-approximation interface as a supplier gap rather than assuming it is already in the pinned library.

nodes.title: Graded Hurwitz homology modules
nodes.statement: For p>=0 define M_p=direct_sum_(n>=0) H_p(Hur_n;k), internally graded by n. Give it the left R-action induced by the degree-zero part of homology multiplication under gluing. Then M_0=R as a graded left module, and simultaneous G-conjugation is an action on M_p compatible with the R-action and U. In each fixed n its homology is finite dimensional by the finite-cell bound in HS.5; that finiteness is not used to define M_p.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Apply the cross product H0(Hur_m;k) tensor Hp(Hur_n;k)->Hp(Hur_(m+n);k) and the induced gluing map.
Associativity and the empty tuple give the module axioms; degree-zero identification gives M0=R.

nodes.title: The Borel arc resolution
nodes.statement: For each n form the semisimplicial space X(n)_q=EB_n×_(B_n)(A(n)_q×c^n) and its thick realization X(n). Its augmentation to Hur_n has, in the covering-bundle model, fibre |A(n)|. For n>=2 the augmentation induces an isomorphism H_t(X(n);k)->H_t(Hur_n;k) whenever t<n-2. Its skeletal filtration is bounded by n-1 in the semisimplicial direction.

Apply connectivity-to-homology and the homology spectral sequence of this actual fibre bundle to obtain the stated safe isomorphism range. Use the finite-dimensional skeletal filtration for the next node.

nodes.statement: For 0<=q<n, X(n)_q is homotopy equivalent to c^n//L_q and then to c^(q+1)×Hur_(n-q-1). This gives H_p(X(n)_q;k) ≅ (K(M_p)_(q+1))_n. Under these identifications the face induced by bL_q->b s_(q,i)L_(q-1) acts on tuples by s_(q,i)^-1; it removes g_i from the first q+1 entries and prefixes g_i^(g_(i+1)...g_q) to the residual tuple. Thus the alternating face differential is exactly K differential.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Use equivariant induction B_n/L_q to identify the Borel term with c^n//L_q. The tail subgroup fixes the first q+1 entries and acts on the remaining entries by the parent Hurwitz action.
On EB_n×_(L_q)c^n a face is (e,g)->(e s_(q,i),s_(q,i)^-1 g). The change in the EB_n coordinate is freely homotopic to the identity at this stage; the inverse braid action is essential.

It converges to H_(p+q)(X(n);k). For p+q<n-2 its abutment identifies with H_(p+q)(Hur_n;k). For q>0, E2_(q,p)=(H_(q+1)K(M_p))_n; E2_(0,p)=coker(K(M_p)_2->K(M_p)_1)_n.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Specialize the supplier skeletal filtered-chain construction to X(n). Use rows from the comparison and its signed face differential.
The filtration has finitely many q for fixed n; prove convergence to X(n) first. Then apply the augmentation only in the valid total-degree range.
Taking row homology gives H_(q+1)K for q>0. The missing K0 is accounted for by the edge map below, rather than inserted into the nonaugmented page.

In the range p<n-2 its image and kernel are determined by the abutment filtration and incoming spectral-sequence differentials.

nodes.title: Uniform degree bounds for Hurwitz homology
nodes.statement: For every p,q>=0, deg H_q(K(M_p))<=A2+A0(3p+q), with constants chosen independently of k. For p>0 one has the stronger low-degree bounds deg H_0 K(M_p),deg H_1 K(M_p)<=A2+3A0 p.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Induct on p. For p=0, M0=R and the regular K bound applies; A0>=1 absorbs its slope.

For p=P>0 and n>A2+3A0 P, the induction hypothesis kills incoming E2_(j,P+1-j) for j>=2: their degrees are <=A2+A0(3P+4-2j). It also kills other total-P filtration pieces E2_(j,P-j) for j>=1: their degrees are <=A2+A0(3P+1-2j).
Since A1>=1 gives A2>=2,A0>=7, the same n satisfies P<n-2. Thus E2_(0,P) maps isomorphically onto (M_P)_n. The exact edge sequence kills both low K groups there.
Apply the linear K bound for q>1. For q=0,1 the preceding stronger bounds imply the displayed uniform estimate.

nodes.title: Marked Hurwitz homological stability
nodes.statement: For finite G and a nonsplitting class c, choose the actual central sum U_D and let a=Dd. There exist nonnegative integers A,B depending only on (G,c), independent of all fields k with |G| invertible, such that U_D:H_p(Hur_n;k)->H_p(Hur_(n+a);k) is an isomorphism whenever n>Ap+B, for every p,n>=0. For the fixed group the proof permits A=3A0 and B=A2+A0+2; these may subsequently be enlarged for the subgroup induction. U_D is the k-linear sum of power-block gluing maps.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Use b=A2+3A0 p as a common cutoff for the two low K groups. The module stability criterion gives isomorphisms for n>=b+A0.
The stated conservative A,B ensure this inequality for every nonnegative p; all data were chosen from finite sets and integral matrices before the coefficient field.
acceptance: No single degree-one branch insertion is asserted to be stable.
No positive-characteristic field dividing |G|, and no integral homology coefficient ring, is included.

nodes.title: Full-monodromy Hurwitz stability
nodes.statement: Choose D simultaneously for all subgroups generated by their intersections with c. After enlarging A,B depending only on (G,c), the same U_D restricts to an isomorphism H_p(CHur_n;k)->H_p(CHur_(n+a);k) for n>Ap+B. The diagonal operator on the exact-H monodromy stratum is U_H=sum_(g∈c∩H) r_g^(Dd), viewed in the component ring for (H,c∩H). There is no factor |c|/|c∩H|.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Decompose marked Hur_n as the disjoint union of exact-generated-subgroup subcovers. U sends an H-stratum only to supergroups of H. Its diagonal part consists exactly of summands with g in H.

Induct on |G|. Proper exact-H diagonal blocks are the full-monodromy stability operators for (H,c∩H); empty or nongenerating intersections contribute zero. Choose a common multiple of all finite permutation exponents and common maxima of their linear ranges, before coefficients.

The quotient by the full-G subspace has a finite filtration with these proper diagonal blocks. Their isomorphisms and marked stability imply the full-G kernel isomorphism. Choose final A,B as maxima of the finitely many subgroup ranges.
acceptance: For the one-element group, full monodromy equals all monodromy, including n=0.
For nontrivial G the empty tuple is excluded from CHur_0.

nodes.title: Homology of the simultaneous-conjugation quotient
nodes.statement: For X=Hur_n or CHur_n, with finite G and |G| invertible in k, the comparison X//G->X/G induces a homology isomorphism and H_p(X/G;k) ≅ H_p(X;k)_G. On an exact-H tuple stratum the point stabilizer is C_G(H). On CHur_n it is Z(G), so the G-action on CHur_n is free if G is center-free. There is no claim that the G-action on all Hur_n is free.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Group the exact-H strata into conjugacy orbits. Each block is G×_(N_G(H)) X_H. The centralizer C_G(H) fixes X_H pointwise, and N_G(H)/C_G(H) acts freely, because point stabilizers are exactly the centralizer.

For this block the Borel-to-ordinary comparison has acyclic BC_G(H) fibre; finite-group averaging and the Cartan–Leray comparison give the homology isomorphism. Assemble the blocks. This avoids asserting one globally constant fibre bundle when centralizers change between components.
The G-homology spectral sequence collapses to coinvariants because |G| is invertible. On full monodromy substitute H=G.
acceptance: Keep the point stabilizer distinct from the normalizer that preserves an entire exact-H stratum.

sources.match: Identifies quotient homology through finite stabilizers of marked tuples. The target supplies a stratumwise Borel argument when centralizers vary.

hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: G-invariance of the central sum and equivariance of gluing make marked stabilization a morphism of k[G]-modules.

Apply coinvariants to the marked isomorphisms and use the finite-quotient comparison. Retain the center-free hypothesis of the exported theorem even though the quotient comparison itself holds more generally.

nodes.title: A finite-cell model for Hurwitz covers
nodes.statement: For n>=2 construct the type-A Salvetti model Z_n of Conf_n using W=S_n with adjacent transpositions S={s_1,...,s_(n-1)}. Let P_n consist of (w,T), w∈W,T⊆S. Its strict order is (w,T)<(v,U) when T is a proper subset of U, w^-1 v belongs to the parabolic subgroup W_U, and length(t w^-1 v)>length(w^-1 v) for every t∈T. Define Z_n=|orderComplex(P_n)|/W for the free left W-action. Give it the coarser CW structure with one q-cell for each q-element T⊆S, using the corresponding parabolic permutohedra as characteristic cells. Establish Z_n≃Conf_n. Set Z_0 and Z_1 to a point. Lift this model along each parent finite covering Hur_n, CHur_n and their unmarked quotients of Conf_n; each lifted model has at most (2|G|)^n cells.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Specialize the Charney–Davis construction to the finite reflection group S_n. Its braid arrangement complement modulo S_n is Conf_n, with a harmless contractible translation coordinate. The invariant good cover and nerve construction in §§1.4–1.5 give the W-equivariant homotopy equivalence to the order-complex model. No general Artin K(pi,1) conjecture is used.

For each T the lower interval is the face poset of the corresponding parabolic permutohedron (a product of convex permutohedra for consecutive blocks). Its boundary is a sphere and its cell a ball. This realizes the coarsening and the quotient attaching maps; use the supplier finite-CW and good-cover interfaces explicitly requested below.

The quotient has sum_q binomial(n-1,q)=2^(n-1)<=2^n cells. Pull back the parent finite covering along the homotopy equivalence and lift cells. Each fibre has size <=|c|^n<=|G|^n, including connected and unmarked subcovers.
acceptance: The general Coxeter/Artin Salvetti theory is outside this target: only the explicit finite type-A construction and cover bound are planned.

nodes.title: A uniform field Betti bound
nodes.statement: Let A,B,a be the common nonnegative integer stability constants for the four spaces, and put K=2|G|, C=K^(A+B+a+1). For center-free finite G and nonsplitting c, every permitted coefficient field k and every i,n>=0 satisfy dim_k H_i(CHur_n/G;k)<=C^(i+1). The same argument bounds the other three variants with the appropriate marked or unmarked stability hypotheses. The constants depend only on (G,c).
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: Every fixed-n Betti number is <=K^n by the cellular chain count.

If n>Ai+B, repeatedly use inverse stabilization to reach an m in the same residue class modulo a with m<=Ai+B+a; if n is already below the threshold keep m=n. Every forward map inverted has a valid source degree.
Then K^m<=K^((A+B+a+1)(i+1))=C^(i+1). This proof only uses field-independent ranges, so C is also independent of coefficients.
acceptance: Respect the residue class modulo a; degree-one stabilization is not available.

nodes.title: Uniform etale Betti numbers
nodes.statement: Assume G is finite and center-free, c is a rational nonidentity single generating nonsplitting conjugacy class, q is a prime power with characteristic coprime to |G|, and L is a prime with L>max(|G|,q,n). For the parent arithmetic Hurwitz scheme Hn_(G,n)^c of connected tame G-covers of the affine line, allowing ramification or no ramification at infinity as in IG.5, there is C=C(G,c) such that dim_(Q_L) H_et^i(Hn_(G,n)^c over algebraic_closure(F_q),Q_L)<=C^(i+1) for every i,n>=0. The same bound holds with F_L coefficients. This is a dimension theorem; its proof supplies no Frobenius-equivariant stabilization.
hypotheses: The standing hypotheses and grading conventions apply; hypotheses weakened or added in the statement take precedence.
proofSteps: For the fixed original n, use the parent analytic/mod-L comparison to CHur_n/G. Its hypotheses include L>max(|G|,q,n), rational c, and tame characteristic. The arithmetic scheme and comparison are imports, not rebuilt here.

Apply the uniform topological field Betti bound with k=F_L. If reduction to smaller m is expanded, all intermediate degrees are <=n and hence the same L suffices; no comparison at n+a is needed for this bound.

Use the parent compatible coefficient-tower comparison and the universal-coefficient rank inequality to pass from mod-L dimension to Q_L dimension, with finite generation and inverse limits explicitly inherited.
Do not derive a Frobenius-equivariant U or fixed-q limiting Cohen–Lenstra distribution: the imported comparisons are fixed-degree, and U is a sum of nonalgebraic gluing maps.
acceptance: An individual stabilization between n and n+a would require L>max(|G|,q,n+a) if expressed through the fixed-degree comparisons.
Do not require the single class to be rational for the purely topological stability theorem.

sources.match: Combines the topological bound with fixed-n arithmetic comparisons and the coefficient tower. The final remark limits the conclusion to Betti dimensions, without Frobenius compatibility.
